info.title: sf-mod-check
info.description: Read-only, offline checks of Starfield mods: plugin checks (structure, FormIDs, links, conditions, scenes, deleted and identical-to-master records), whole load-order conflicts, release-zip checks, and triage: a first-pass report on a downloaded mod. Formerly sfmodcheck.

options.name: --data
options.description: the game's Data folder, for the EditorIDs of records in the masters (default: Steam's usual folder)

options.name: --json
options.description:
the report as JSON instead of text (always complete); on stdout the RESULT line follows
the JSON, so use --out for a file that holds only the JSON

options.name: --out
options.description: write the report to this file (stdout then gets only the RESULT line)

options.name: --all
options.description:
list everything in the text report (long lists are cut short otherwise), and each cell's records
Records whose bytes differ but whose fields are all equal count as noise, which is no difference.
Scripts and script properties are matched by name, so a new order alone is noise.
exit 0 = no real differences (noise only counts as none), 1 = differences, 2 = bad input or setup

options.name: --type
options.description: keep only records of this four-letter type, for example LCTN, MISC, NPC_

options.name: --plugin
options.description:
read only this plugin and its masters, with no Plugins.txt; with no record given, list every record
the plugin holds. Masters are looked for in the plugin's own folder, then each --masters-dir, then --data.
Give the record as an EditorID or FormKey: a console FormID needs the whole load order.

options.name: --masters-dir
options.description: another folder that holds the plugin's masters (can be given more than once)

options.name: --max
options.description:
with --plugin and no record: list at most this many records (default 100; 0 lists them all);
with --refs: list at most this many referring records (default 100; 0 lists them all)

options.name: --full
options.description:
print every nested value of the winning copy as an indented tree (zeros included) instead of the
main fields; --json adds it as "tree"

options.name: --versions
options.description:
list every copy of the record in load order and what each copy changes against the copy it was
built on; --json adds it as "versions" (needs a record: not with the --plugin listing)

options.name: --refs
--data
options.description: the game's Data folder (default: Steam's usual folder)

options.name: --masters-dir
options.description: another folder to look for masters in (can be given more than once)

options.name: --quiet
options.description: no byline, and no WARNING lines when there are errors

options.name: --verbose
options.description:
the troubleshooting log on stderr, or in that file
The last line is RESULT: OK (0 errors, n warnings), RESULT: FAIL (n errors, n warnings) or RESULT: CANNOT CHECK (...).
exit 0 = no errors (warnings allowed), 1 = errors, 2 = can't check (a missing plugin or master, a bad argument)

options.name: --plugin
options.description: read only this plugin and its masters (found in its folder, then each --masters-dir, then --data)

options.name: --compare
options.description:
count another NPC's lines per type too (for example a vanilla companion) and mark the types this
NPC has none of as missing; the same forms as the NPC

options.name: --type
options.description: keep only lines of this Category (Combat) or Category / Subtype ("Combat / Hit"); letter case ignored

options.name: --max
options.description: list at most this many lines (default 200; 0 lists them all); the counts are always complete

options.name: --no-files
options.description: don't look for the voice and lip files (faster; wem and lip show ?)

options.name: --json
options.description: print one JSON object with every line

commands.name: check
commands.description: (is a patch still up to date? sf-mod-check patch check --help)

options.name: --out
options.description: write the list to this file (default: the screen, stdout)

options.name: --voice
options.description: a voice type (EditorID) for the lines that name none; may be given more than once

options.name: --utf8
options.description: write UTF-8 (default: Windows-1252, what the Creation Kit writes and Voice Cloner reads)
